name: Citizenship by Birth or Descent

qualifying_event.description: Citizenship is conferred automatically at birth: either by birth in Saint Lucia (jus soli, with narrow diplomatic/wartime exceptions) or by descent from a citizen parent for births abroad.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Birth certificate; for descent cases, proof of the citizen parent's own citizenship and how it was acquired.

requirements.blocker_text: Automatic citizenship for anyone born in Saint Lucia after the appointed date (independence), EXCEPT where neither parent is a citizen and the father has diplomatic immunity, or where the father is a citizen of a country at war with Saint Lucia and the birth occurs in enemy-occupied territory.

requirement_groups.name: Born abroad to a citizen parent

requirements.blocker_text: Born outside Saint Lucia to a mother OR father who is a citizen at the time of the birth, provided that parent's own citizenship was NOT itself acquired by descent under this same provision or under Section 3(2) -- i.e. descent-based citizenship does not chain across multiple generations born abroad.

evidence_required.document: Parent's proof of citizenship and its basis of acquisition (descent cases)

sources.title: Citizenship of Saint Lucia Act, Section 4 (primary legislation): Acquisition of Citizenship by Birth -- jus soli by birth in Saint Lucia after the appointed date, with diplomatic-immunity and enemy-occupation exceptions

Citizenship of Saint Lucia Act, Section 5 (primary legislation): Persons Born Outside Saint Lucia After the Appointed Date -- citizenship by descent from either a citizen mother or father, one-generation-only limit (excludes parents whose own citizenship derives from this same section or Section 3(2))

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Saint Lucia's initial build. Two notable features confirmed directly from the primary Act text: (1) Saint Lucia's jus soli rule (Section 4) is broader/simpler than the Bahamas' equivalent -- there is no post-1973-style cutoff date complication and no gender asymmetry in the exceptions (both exceptions turn on the FATHER's status specifically -- diplomatic immunity or enemy nationality -- which is itself a residual gender-specific drafting quirk worth flagging, though it only narrows an otherwise near-universal jus soli rule rather than gating it); (2) the descent rule (Section 5) is explicitly GENDER-NEUTRAL (either the mother or the father transmitting citizenship) and, like Trinidad and Tobago's equivalent, caps at one generation born abroad -- a grandchild of a citizen born abroad to a parent who is themselves a citizen only by descent does NOT qualify.
